skill.name: web-fetch
skill.description: Fetches web pages as clean markdown by checking markdown responses first, then using selector-based HTML extraction and a Bun fallback parser.
skill.summary: Fetches documentation and article pages as clean markdown.
skill.author: 0xBigBoss

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick findings are false positives from Markdown formatting and TypeScript template literals. Confirmed risks are expected network access, shell workflows around user supplied URLs, and package manager execution for setup; the highest contextual concern is untrusted URL handling in shell commands.

remediation.issue: User supplied URLs are used in shell command examples.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer the Bun script or another argument-array based helper for URL handling. If shell examples remain, require strict URL validation and escaping before substitution.

remediation.issue: The fallback script fetches any command line URL.
remediation.suggestion: Validate URLs before fetching. Allow only http and https, block localhost, private IP ranges, link-local addresses, and cloud metadata endpoints.

remediation.issue: Setup instructions run bun install for a community skill.
remediation.suggestion: Commit a lockfile or document exact dependency versions and integrity checks. Avoid lifecycle scripts and explain that dependencies are downloaded during setup.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted URL Used in Shell Workflows
semantic_findings.description: The skill documentation repeatedly places a user supplied URL into shell commands. If an agent substitutes a malicious URL without strict escaping, command injection or unintended shell behavior is possible.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The shell examples consistently use a placeholder URL in command strings, and no validation or escaping rule is documented. The risk depends on how the agent substitutes the URL, so confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Outbound URL Fetch
semantic_findings.description: The fallback script accepts a command line URL and fetches it without an allowlist, scheme restriction, or private network guard. This can be abused to request internal services from the agent environment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The URL is read directly from process.argv and passed to fetch. The file contains no host, scheme, localhost, private IP, or metadata endpoint checks before the request.

content.user_title: Fetch Web Pages as Clean Markdown
content.value_statement: Web pages often include navigation, scripts, and noisy layout. This skill fetches documentation and articles as clean markdown for review, citation, and reuse.
actual_capabilities: Checks content type headers and prefers markdown-native responses.
Converts selected HTML regions to markdown with include and exclude selectors.
Provides selector patterns for Anthropic docs, MDN, GitHub docs, and generic pages.
Runs a Bun fallback parser using linkedom and Turndown when selector output is poor.
Removes common navigation, script, style, sidebar, and copy button elements.
Preserves fenced code blocks when converting HTML documentation.
limitations: Requires curl, html2markdown, Bun, and local dependencies for the full workflow.
Cannot extract content from pages that only render meaningful text with client-side JavaScript.
Selector quality depends on each site structure and may need manual adjustment.
Fetches user supplied URLs, so users must avoid private or untrusted network targets.

use_cases.title: Collect Documentation for Agents
use_cases.description: Fetch a documentation page and return clean markdown that an AI agent can read and summarize.

use_cases.title: Convert Articles for Research Notes
use_cases.description: Extract an article body without navigation, ads, scripts, or repeated page chrome.

use_cases.title: Debug HTML Extraction Rules
use_cases.description: Test selectors and fallback parsing when a site has unusual content containers.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch One Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single trusted URL.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch this documentation page as clean markdown: https://example.com/docs/page. Keep headings, links, and code blocks.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Article Text
prompt_templates.scenario: Use selector-based cleanup for a noisy page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch this article and remove navigation, sidebars, scripts, and footers. Return only the main readable content as markdown.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Selector
prompt_templates.scenario: Check whether a specific HTML region gives better output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch this page using the main article selector. If output is incomplete, try the generic main content selector and compare results.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Reference Digest
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow across multiple trusted documentation pages.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch these three trusted documentation URLs, convert each to clean markdown, and summarize the differences in their setup steps.

output_examples.output: A markdown document with the page title, section headings, body text, links, and preserved code block formatting.
A clean article body without menus, headers, footers, scripts, or repeated sidebar content.

output_examples.input: Try a selector on an unfamiliar page.
output_examples.output: A short extraction result that shows whether the selector captured the main content or needs adjustment.

best_practices: Use trusted http or https URLs and avoid private network addresses.
Check headers first when a page may already provide markdown.
Start with known selectors, then test generic article or main selectors.
anti_patterns: Do not fetch URLs supplied by an untrusted party without review.
Do not assume client-rendered pages will contain extractable HTML content.
Do not run setup commands without checking dependency versions and source.

faq.question: What does this skill fetch?
faq.answer: It fetches web pages and converts readable documentation or article content into markdown.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it handle JavaScript-rendered pages?
faq.answer: No. It cannot extract content that only appears after browser-side JavaScript runs.

faq.question: Why does it need Bun?
faq.answer: Bun runs the fallback TypeScript parser when curl and selector conversion produce poor output.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: The full workflow expects curl, html2markdown, Bun, and the local package dependencies.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with any URL?
faq.answer: No. Use trusted public URLs and avoid private, internal, or sensitive network locations.
